chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu'l-Husayn al-Kufi al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to me. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Yazid narrated to us. He said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them all). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Four people torment the inhabitants of the Fire beyond what they are already suffering. They drink from the boiling water and blazing fire, crying out in woe and destruction. The inhabitants of the Fire say to one another: 'What is wrong with these four who torment us beyond what we already suffer?' One is suspended in a coffin of embers; one drags his intestines; one has pus and blood flowing from his mouth; and one eats his own flesh. It is said to the companion of the coffin: 'What did this wretch do to torment us beyond what we already suffer?' He says: 'This wretch died while he owed debts to people and did not find it in himself to repay or fulfill them.' Then it is said to the one dragging his intestines: 'What did this wretch do to torment us beyond what we already suffer?' He says: 'This wretch did not care where urine touched his body.' Then it is said to the one with pus and blood flowing from his mouth: 'What did this wretch do to torment us beyond what we already suffer?' He says: 'This wretch would mimic — he would look for every vile word, then spread it and imitate it.' Then it is said to the one eating his own flesh: 'What did this wretch do to torment us beyond what we already suffer?' He says: 'This wretch would consume the flesh of people through backbiting and walk about spreading gossip.'

key_terms.الأبعد: Literally 'the further/distant one' — a pejorative expression used in classical Arabic to refer to a condemned or wretched person
key_terms.الجحيم: The blazing fire / Hell — a specific level or name for Hell
key_terms.الحميم: Boiling water — one of the punishments of Hell mentioned in the Quran
key_terms.الحميم والجحيم: Boiling water and blazing fire — two distinct Hellfire punishments often paired in eschatological texts
key_terms.الغيبة: Backbiting — speaking ill of an absent person; explicitly forbidden in the Quran (49:12)
key_terms.النميمة: Gossip/tale-bearing — carrying speech between people to cause discord; a major sin in Islamic ethics
key_terms.الويل والثبور: Woe and destruction — expressions of lamentation in Hellfire; 'wail' invokes Quran 25:13

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of sinners who will cause extra suffering in Hell according to a hadith of the Prophet?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) describes four sinners whose punishments in Hell are so severe that they torment even the other damned souls around them. Each punishment directly mirrors the sin: the debtor who refused to repay is suspended in embers, the one who neglected ritual purity drags his intestines, the spreader of vile speech bleeds pus and blood, and the backbiter and gossipmonger eats his own flesh. This eschatological teaching, transmitted through Imam Ali and the chain of Imams to al-Sadiq, vividly illustrates the gravity of debt, ritual impurity, slander, backbiting, and gossip in Islamic ethics.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ja`far Abu'l Husayn al-Kufi al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Musa b. `Imran al-Nakha`i narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Yazid narrated to me. He said: Hafs b. Ghiyath narrated to me from Ja`far b. Muhammad from his forefathers from `Ali (as). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) said: Four people harm the people of the Fire due to the way they are being harmed. They will be feeding from the boiling water and Hell, calling out to one another in woe and punishment. The people of the Fire will say to one another: “What is with these four who harm us on top of what we are already being harmed by?” One will be attached to a coffin of embers, one will have his intestines dragging, one vomits pus and blood, and one will be eating his own flesh. So, it will be said to the companion of the coffin: “What did the further one do for him to harm us on top of what we are already being harmed by?” So, he will say: “The further one died whilst he had the wealth of the people on his neck (debt). He did not find it in himself to pay it or fulfil it.” Then, it will be said to the one with his intestines dragging: “What did the further one do for him to harm us on top of what we are already being harmed by?” So, he will say: “The further one did not care (purify) where urine was on his body.” Then, it will be said to the one vomiting pus and blood: “What did the further one do for him to harm us on top of what we are already being harmed by?” So, he will say: “The further one would mimic. He would look to every filthy word, then support it and mimic it.” Then, it will be said to the one eating his own flesh: “What did the further one do for him to harm us on top of what we are already being harmed by?” So, he will say: “The further one would eat the flesh of the people through backbiting and gossip.”
